articles.title: Judge slams Justice Department for asking her to ‘disbelieve’ Trump in golf course case
articles.summary: A federal judge extended an order blocking tree removal from a Washington, DC golf course President Donald Trump is seeking to renovate, while imposing new n...
articles.body:
A federal judge extended an order blocking tree removal from a Washington, DC golf course President Donald Trump is seeking to renovate, while imposing new notice requirements on any other major changes the administration seeks to make on the golf course grounds.

The new 70-page opinion from US District Judge Ana Reyes cited Trump's own statements about his plans for East Potomac Golf Course.

The judge said she was forced to act now in the long-simmering dispute – which came to a head in recent weeks because the administration cut down 400-plus trees on the grounds with little notice – "because the Government did what it assured all it would not do."

The ruling is a major setback for Trump's efforts to turn the beloved but modest public golf course into a championship level course. It also sets the stage for an appeals court battle in a case that had produced sharp confrontations between the administration and the judiciary.

The new ruling comes after a showdown between the Trump administration and the federal bench in DC during a marathon hearing last week over the president's efforts to overhaul the course.

Tensions were ratcheted up for those proceedings when Trump posted to social media that construction would begin at the course "immediately," while calling Reyes a "crazed lunatic."

"The events surrounding this case have become extraordinary," Reyes wrote Monday. The way the Trump administration rushed to chop down hundreds of trees was "concerning," she said.

"The Government appears to have set the timing of the tree removal and late notice to impede Plaintiffs' ability to seek Court intervention," Reyes wrote. "And its recent actions call into question other representations it has made to the Court over these many months."

Reyes said she was reserving judgment on whether the government purposely misled her. But she indicated she is considering issuing a preservation order for all DOJ communications regarding the tree removal – a signal she may further probe the conduct of the government's attorneys.

Under Reyes' order, the administration cannot take any action to cut down, alter or harm additional trees on the grounds – unless to protect public safety, and in those cases, it must give detailed notice to the court. The Trump administration must also give 10 days notice for any plans to close the golf course or if it plans to make "irreversible" alterations to the course's design, Reyes said.

Just before midnight Monday, Trump railed on Truth Social about Reyes' ruling, while continuing to vow he will close the course on November 15 to renovate it.

"The judge does not have the Constitutional Right to 'ask for or receive notices,' which are time-consuming, unnecessary, expensive, and unconstitutional. We will immediately appeal this decision," Trump said in the post. "To have to give advanced notices to a judge who has no expertise in Golf, Architecture, Landscaping, Construction, or anything else having to do with building such a World Class Project, is not fair, appropriate, or Constitutional."

The lawsuit was brought by historic preservationists and individual golfers who alleged the administration was violating environmental law in how it planned to carry out Trump's wishes to renovate East Potomac Golf Course – which for decades has offered affordable golf access to DC residents. Trump's plans for the course would likely make it far more difficult to access and expensive to play, while eliminating much of the public park space that surrounds it.

The new decision stems from the October 10 move by the administration to chop down hundreds of trees from the grounds. In the months and even days before the mass tree removal, administration officials had claimed that the proposals for Trump's renovation were still in their infancy, and there were no imminent plans for making major changes to the course.

After chopping down more than 400 trees, the administration continued to argue that the tree removals were separate from the overhaul Trump was planning and were instead the product of a 2019 proposal to make the course look more like it did when it was first built.

Reyes had expressed deep skepticism of that explanation. She had initially issued a temporary restraining order blocking all tree removal and requiring three days' notice of any other major changes to the course. That TRO was set to expire on Monday.

In her latest opinion, Reyes concluded that she would trust Trump's own public statements that renovations were beginning "immediately" over what government officials had claimed in court.

The Justice Department, she wrote, "asks the Court to disbelieve repeated public comments made by the President, who has stated in no uncertain terms that DOI and Secretary Burgum have a plan to redesign the Course."

Reyes devoted a significant portion of her opinion Monday to defending the judiciary's ability to serve as a check on the executive branch.

"One branch may not shield itself from accountability merely by invoking separation of powers principles without any reasoning. But that is all the Government has done," she wrote.

This story has been updated with additional details.

articles.title: 'Dia de Finados': confira o que abre e fecha no Oeste Paulista | G1
articles.standfirst: Repartições municipais terão alterações nesta sexta-feira (30), devido ao ponto facultativo do Dia do Servidor Público, e na segunda-feira (2), feriado nacional de Finados.
articles.summary: O ponto facultativo nesta sexta-feira (30) e o feriado de Finados na segunda-feira (2) alteram o funcionamento de serviços públicos no Oeste Paulista.
articles.body:
Calçadão no Centro de Presidente Prudente (SP) — Foto: Arquivo/Secom

O ponto facultativo do Dia do Servidor Público, transferido para esta sexta-feira (30), e o feriado nacional de Finados, celebrado na segunda-feira (2), alteram o funcionamento de serviços públicos em cidades do Oeste Paulista.

Em Presidente Prudente (SP), Álvares Machado (SP), Adamantina (SP), Dracena (SP) e Osvaldo Cruz (SP), repartições municipais terão horários diferenciados, enquanto serviços essenciais, como coleta de lixo e atendimentos de saúde, seguem cronogramas específicos.

Confira como fica o funcionamento dos serviços em cada município:

A Prefeitura de Presidente Prudente informou que haverá alterações no funcionamento dos serviços municipais entre sexta-feira (30) e segunda-feira (2). O expediente administrativo será retomado na terça-feira (3).

Centro Cultural Matarazzo: o Espaço Boulevard ficará aberto para visitação durante o feriado e o fim de semana, das 16h às 22h.

Balneário da Amizade: permanecerá aberto no horário habitual, das 6h às 21h.

Bom Prato: funcionará normalmente na sexta-feira (30) e ficará fechado na segunda-feira (2).

Coleta de lixo: será realizada normalmente na sexta-feira (30) e no sábado (31). Na segunda-feira (2), não haverá coleta.

Varrição: na sexta-feira (30) e no sábado (31), o serviço será realizado somente no Parque do Povo e na região central (sexta-feira tem funcionamento normal e sábado tem atendimento das 9h às 15h).

Comércio: segunda-feira (2) estará fechado.

Plantão de vacinação: será realizado no sábado (31), na Estratégia Saúde da Família (ESF) Vila Marcondes, das 8h às 14h.

UBSs e ESFs: permanecerão fechadas, com exceção do plantão de vacinação informado.

UPA Zona Norte, no Jardim Guanabara: atendimento 24 horas.

Pronto Atendimento Cohab: na sexta-feira (30), das 19h às 7h; no sábado (31) e no domingo (1º), atendimento 24 horas; na segunda-feira (2), das 19h às 7h.

Pronto Atendimento Santana: na sexta-feira (30), das 19h às 7h; no sábado (31) e no domingo (1º), atendimento 24 horas; na segunda-feira (2), das 19h às 7h.

Farmácia Central: funcionará de sexta-feira (30) a segunda-feira (2), das 7h às 19h.

Farmácias dos Prontos Atendimentos Cohab e Santana: funcionarão no sábado (31) e no domingo (1º), das 7h às 19h.

A Prefeitura de Álvares Machado e as divisões municipais que funcionam fora do Paço terão alterações no atendimento durante o período. Na terça-feira (3) o expediente será normal.

Prefeitura: sexta-feira (30) e na segunda-feira (2) estará fechada.

Poupatempo: sexta-feira (30) e na sábado (31) terá expediente normal. Na segunda-feira (2), estará fechado.

Educação: não haverá aulas na sexta-feira (30) e na segunda-feira (2).

Unidades de saúde: de sexta-feira (30) a segunda-feira (2) estarão fechadas.

Dispensários de medicamentos: - Sede: estará fechada na sexta-feira (30), no domingo (1º) e na segunda-feira (2). No sábado (31), haverá plantão das 7h às 16h. - Parque dos Pinheiros: fechado de sexta-feira (30) a segunda-feira (2). - Salvador Costa: fechado de sexta-feira (30) a segunda-feira (2).

Coleta seletiva: será realizada normalmente na sexta-feira (30). Na segunda-feira (2), não haverá coleta.

Central de Ambulância: atendimento normal.

As repartições públicas municipais de Dracena não terão expediente na sexta-feira (30), devido ao ponto facultativo do Dia do Servidor Público, nem na segunda-feira (2), feriado nacional de Finados.

Estratégias Saúde da Família (ESFs): funcionarão normalmente na sexta-feira (30).

Farmácia da ESF Affonso Arthur Vieira Resende, no Jardim Brasilândia: funcionará normalmente na sexta-feira (30).

ESF Irene Kato: terá atendimento noturno na sexta-feira (30), das 18h às 22h.

Demais unidades e serviços de saúde: não terão atendimento na sexta-feira (30). Estão incluídos a farmácia do Centro de Saúde I (Postão), a sala de vacinas, o Centro de Saúde e as UBSs José Serafim Barbosa e Antônio Dias Pedroso. As unidades de saúde permanecerão fechadas. O atendimento será mantido exclusivamente pelo Pronto Atendimento Municipal (PAM).

Coleta de lixo: o serviço será normal na sexta-feira (30) e na segunda-feira (2).

A Prefeitura de Osvaldo Cruz informou que alguns serviços municipais funcionarão normalmente nesta sexta-feira (30), enquanto os demais setores ligados à administração municipal estarão fechados.

Serviços que funcionarão normalmente na sexta-feira (30):

Transporte para faculdades, nas instituições que tiverem aulas;

Transporte para as EMEIs Francisca Dassi e Rodolfo Zaros;

Coleta seletiva, conforme o cronograma habitual de sexta-feira;

Posto de Saúde do Jardim Primavera, das 7h às 13h;

Farmácia Municipal Central, na Avenida Kennedy, das 7h às 13h;

Os demais setores ligados à Prefeitura estarão fechados nesta sexta-feira (30).

O atendimento nos setores municipais será retomado normalmente na terça-feira (3). A Prefeitura orienta quem precisar dos serviços a se programar e buscar atendimento nos dias anteriores ao ponto facultativo.

A Prefeitura de Adamantina transferiu o ponto facultativo do Dia do Servidor Público, inicialmente previsto para quarta-feira (28), para sexta-feira (30).

Repartições públicas: não haverá expediente nas repartições municipais abrangidas pelo decreto na sexta-feira e na segunda-feira (2), feriado de Finados. O atendimento administrativo será retomado na terça-feira (3).

Serviços essenciais: a medida não se aplica às repartições que prestam serviços essenciais ou cujas atividades não podem ser interrompidas.

articles.title: Reconhecido por Lula após atuação na campanha, Janones se reúne com petista para traçar futuro: 'Precisa de força no Congresso' | G1
articles.standfirst: Ventilado como possível ministro do governo Lula 4, parlamentar disse considerar que pode 'ajudar muito como deputado'. Janones coordenou canal 'Exército do Lula' nas eleições.
articles.summary: Ventilado como possível ministro do governo Lula 4, parlamentar disse considerar que pode 'ajudar muito como deputado'. Janones coordenou canal 'Exército do Lula' nas eleições.
articles.body:
O deputado federal André Janones (Avante-MG) se reuniu nesta quinta-feira (29) com o presidente reeleito Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), para um almoço no Palácio da Alvorada.

Em entrevista, Janones avaliou que considera ser mais útil ao governo no Congresso Nacional do que à frente de um ministério.

Mas ponderou que a definição sobre seu papel na próxima gestão será discutida com Lula e que fará o que o presidente decidir.

"A gente vai entender onde posso somar mais com o Lula 4. Por vontade própria, não entendo que um ministério é onde posso ajudar mais, mas estou na liderança dele", declarou.

Janones disse ainda que Lula deve precisar de força no Congresso, que terá maioria de direita na próxima legislatura.

"Acho que posso ajudar muito como deputado, ele [Lula] precisa de força no congresso, a extrema direita tem maioria e eu posso dar um peso ali. Eu vou seguir o que o presidente mandar." afirmou

Janones também falou sobre a possibilidade de ampliar sua participação no enfrentamento ao que chama de "extrema direita" em outros países, mas não detalhou se já existem convites nesse sentido.

"Tenho desejo gigante de contribuir em todos os lugares que tiver voz no mundo pra ficar livre da extrema direita. A democracia não existe na hegemonia, só não cabem, no tabuleiro, figuras extremistas, que atentam contra o estado democrático" declarou.

Entre as possibilidades citadas, está uma eventual colaboração com o primeiro-ministro da Espanha, Pedro Sánchez, em iniciativas de comunicação e mobilização política.

No Palácio da Alvorada, Janones disse a jornalistas que pretende continuar com o canal "Exército do Lula" no WhatsApp.

A nova meta, segundo o deputado, é chegar a 13 milhões de inscritos até a cerimônia de posse do presidente, marcada para o dia 5 de janeiro.

Atualmente, o canal conta com 10,9 milhões de inscritos. A ferramenta contribuiu para a mobilização digital da campanha de Lula no segundo turno da disputa presidencial.

No discurso da vitória, Lula mencionou Janones, reconhecendo o empenho do aliado para a vitória nas urnas.

Janones abraça o presidente Lula durante discurso após reeleição neste domingo (25). — Foto: LECO VIANA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

articles.title: Acidente de trem na Espanha: brasileira está entre os feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: Itamaraty está prestando assistência à vítima, que acionou os serviços consulares nesta quinta-feira (29). Ao menos 69 pessoas morreram e 110 ficaram feridas no acidente, segundo o governo espanhol.
articles.summary: Acidente de trem na Espanha deixa brasileira ferida e 69 mortos; Itamaraty presta assistência à vítima após falha técnica em linha de alta velocidade.
articles.body:
Uma brasileira está na lista de pessoas feridas no acidente entre dois trens de alta velocidade que colidiram na Espanha , causando ao menos 69 mortes. A informação foi confirmada à TV Globo pelo Ministério das Relações Exteriores (Itamaraty), nesta quinta-feira (29).

O serviço consular do Itamaraty foi acionado ainda na quarta (28), dia do acidente, e a brasileira já sendo assistida.

Segundo informações obtidas pela reportagem, trata-se de uma mulher que sofreu ferimentos. As primeiras informações são que o estado dela não é grave.

Ao menos 69 pessoas morreram e 110 ficaram feridas no acidente, segundo o governo espanhol.

Desses, 50 permanecem internadas no hospital e 15 estão em estado grave. As equipes de emergência foram mobilizadas para atender às vítimas e retirar passageiros dos vagões atingidos.

O acidente ocorreu por volta das 8h54 no horário local (3h54 no horário de Brasília), nas proximidades de Urda, a cerca de 140 km ao sul de Madri.

A causa definitiva ainda não foi esclarecida. Segundo o ministro dos Transportes, o sistema automatizado de gestão de tráfego ferroviário, chamado LZB, parou de funcionar após uma falha de comunicação entre computadores.

O trem da empresa estatal Renfe transportava entre 393 e 397 passageiros, segundo informações divulgadas pelas autoridades. Já o trem da Iryo levava 147 pessoas, incluindo um bebê.

Tudo isso aconteceu em um trecho da linha de alta velocidade que liga a capital espanhola a Sevilha, no sul do país.

articles.title: Quem vai representar a família Bolsonaro na política a partir de 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Michelle, Carlos, Jair Renan e Renato Bolsonaro vão representar a família na política em Brasília a partir de janeiro. Senador deixou o Brasil após perder disputa presidencial para Lula.
articles.summary: Michelle, Carlos, Jair Renan e Renato Bolsonaro vão representar a família na política em Brasília a partir de janeiro. Senador deixou o Brasil após perder disputa presidencial para Lula.
articles.body:
Michelle, Carlos, Renato e Jair Renan Bolsonaro, eleitos para o Congresso Nacional em 2026. — Foto: Isac Nóbrega/PR; NSC TV/Reprodução; Evaristo Sa/AFP/Arquivo; Redes sociais

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) perdeu a eleição presidencial para Lula (PT) por 4,4 milhões de votos e foi embora para os Estados Unidos. Após a fuga, o senador divulgou uma carta em que se autoproclamou "presidente eleito". Depois, publicou uma nova versão em que se autodeclarou "líder do Brasil".

Nos EUA, Flávio se juntou ao irmão Eduardo, que vive lá desde fevereiro de 2025. O ex-deputado perdeu o mandato e foi condenado por tentar interferir no julgamento do pai, Jair Bolsonaro, preso e condenado por tentar dar um golpe de Estado. Eduardo, como o irmão mais velho, diz ser perseguido pela Justiça brasileira.

Derrotado nas urnas e investigado por lavagem de dinheiro, corrupção e evasão de divisas, Flávio Bolsonaro ficará sem cargo político — e sem foro privilegiado — pela primeira vez desde 2003, quando assumiu o primeiro mandato de deputado estadual no Rio de Janeiro.

Assim como Flávio, Eduardo e Jair Bolsonaro também estarão sem mandato. A família, no entanto, será representada a partir de 2027 por quatro integrantes eleitos para o Congresso. Veja quem são:

Michelle Bolsonaro (PL-DF), esposa do ex-presidente, foi eleita senadora pelo Distrito Federal em sua estreia nas urnas. A ex-primeira-dama teve 938.496 votos (29,05%).

Além de conquistar seu mandato, ela ajudou a eleger a aliada Bia Kicis (PL-DF) para a segunda vaga destinada ao DF no Senado.

Michelle Bolsonaro vota em Brasília neste domingo (4). — Foto: REUTERS/Diego Herculano

Carlos Bolsonaro (PL-SC) transferiu o título de eleitor do Rio de Janeiro, onde construiu sua carreira política como vereador, para Santa Catarina. Carlos ficou com a segunda cadeira disponível para o Senado no estado ao obter 1.902.100 votos (25,21%). Em primeiro lugar ficou Carol de Toni (PL-SC), aliada da família.

Carlos Bolsonaro (PL), eleito Senador por Santa Catarina — Foto: NSC TV/Reprodução

O filho mais novo de Jair Bolsonaro foi eleito para a Câmara dos Deputados por Santa Catarina. Jair Renan foi o quarto candidato mais votado no estado, com 131.555 votos. Atualmente, ele é vereador em Balneário Camboriú (SC).

Jair Renan Bolsonaro foi eleito vereador de Bolsonaro — Foto: Divulgação

Irmão mais novo de Jair, Renato Bolsonaro (PL-SP) foi eleito para a Câmara dos Deputados por São Paulo após receber 379.312 votos. Foi o sexto mais votado no estado.

Capitão reformado do Exército, Renato já havia disputado eleições para vereador, prefeito e deputado na região do Vale do Ribeira, em São Paulo. Foi vereador em Praia Grande na década de 1990.

Ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (à esq.) e Renato Bolsonaro (à dir.) — Foto: Redes sociais

Ex-mulher de Jair e mãe de Flávio, Carlos e Eduardo, Rogéria Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) disputou uma vaga na Câmara dos Deputados pelo Rio de Janeiro, recebeu 65.496 votos e não se elegeu. Foi vereadora por dois mandatos no Rio de Janeiro na década de 1990.

Flávio Bolsonaro e a mãe, Rogéria Bolsonaro. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

articles.title: Eleições 2026: 26 partidos reconheceram vitória de Lula nas urnas | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento da TV Globo considera notas oficiais e manifestações públicas de dirigentes e assessorias após o resultado das eleições, e não inclui o PT, partido de Lula.
articles.summary: Levantamento da TV Globo considera notas oficiais e manifestações públicas de dirigentes após o resultado das eleições, e não inclui o PT, partido do presidente eleito.
articles.body:
Vinte e seis partidos políticos divulgaram manifestações em que reconhecem a vitória do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) nas eleições deste ano. O petista conquistou a reeleição contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), que deixou o país após o resultado.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, duas legendas não haviam se manifestado sobre o resultado das eleições: Agir e Mobiliza .

Após desembarcar nos Estados Unidos, Flávio divulgou uma carta com teor golpista, na qual afirmou não reconhecer o resultado das urnas no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, acusou suposta fraude eleitoral e afirmou ser o "verdadeiro presidente do Brasil", o "presidente eleito".

🔎 Depois de divulgar a primeira carta, em formato de imagens, em uma rede social, Flávio divulgou uma nova carta, também em imagens, em que substituiu as expressões "verdadeiro presidente do Brasil" e "presidente eleito" por "líder do Brasil" e "líder".

Segundo levantamento feito pela TV Globo e pelo g1 a partir de notas oficiais, assessorias, e publicações das legendas e de seus dirigentes , 26 partidos reconheceram a vitória do petista; o partido Novo questionou as instituições e afirmou que o país "não é uma democracia"; e outros dois não se manifestaram.

O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) atestou a regularidade do processo eleitoral e reconheceu a vitória do presidente Lula ainda no domingo (25), após a totalização dos votos.

Depois da divulgação da carta de Flávio, questionando o resultado nas urnas, o presidente da Corte Eleitoral, ministro Kassio Nunes Marques e indicado ao cargo de ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) pelo ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL), afirmou que a Justiça Eleitoral entregou o pleito deste ano com segurança e que as eleições "transcorreram dentro da mais absoluta normalidade".

Entre as siglas que reconheceram a vitória estão o PL — partido do candidato derrotado Flávio Bolsonaro —, União Brasil, MDB, PSD, Republicanos, PSDB, PDT, PSB, PSOL, Podemos, Avante, Democrata, Democracia Cristã (DC), UP e PSTU.

(Atualização: após a publicação da reportagem do g1, o Democrata, o Solidariedade, o PP, o PRD e o Democracia Cristã (DC) se manifestaram reconhecendo as eleições e a vitória do presidente Lula. Veja mais abaixo).

O reconhecimento do resultado eleitoral não significa, necessariamente, apoio ao governo eleito. Algumas legendas fizeram manifestações institucionais sobre o resultado, enquanto outras aproveitaram o momento para apresentar críticas políticas ou defender seus próprios projetos.

Segundo o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), o Brasil tem 30 partidos políticos registrados. A relação usada no levantamento reúne 29 siglas, sem incluir o PT , partido de Lula.

Lula em seu último ato na Av. Paulista antes do segundo turno. — Foto: Paulo Pinto/Agência Brasil

Partidos reconheceram a vitória em manifestações públicas

Entre os partidos que se manifestaram estão legendas de diferentes espectros políticos, inclusive algumas que fizeram oposição ao presidente durante a campanha.

O PL, partido do candidato derrotado Flávio Bolsonaro, publicou uma manifestação sobre o resultado. União Brasil, MDB, PSD e Republicanos também defenderam o resultado declarado pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

No campo da oposição, o PSDB também se manifestou. Já partidos como PSOL, PDT, Cidadania, PSB, Podemos, Partido Verde (PV), Rede Sustentabilidade, Unidade Popular (UP) e PSTU publicaram notas ou mensagens relacionadas ao resultado eleitoral.

Em nota, os partidos PT, PCdoB, PV, PSB, PSOL, Rede e PDT afirmaram que "o Brasil não aceita interferência estrangeira em seu processo democrático".

"O candidato derrotado nas eleições fugiu do Brasil para não enfrentar a Justiça brasileira. Não por acaso, o candidato derrotado buscou abrigo justamente junto a Trump, que atuou abertamente para interferir em nossas eleições", afirmaram os partidos.

"A contestação do resultado não se sustenta. A prorrogação do horário de votação foi pedida pelas duas campanhas, PT e PL, por restrição em transportes públicos e chuvas fortes, e concedida de forma isonômica a todo o país", disseram as siglas.

O União Brasil , que declarou apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno, defendeu o reconhecimento do resultado da eleição e afirmou que "é hora de encerrar a disputa".

"A eleição de 25 de outubro transcorreu com lisura e o seu resultado deve ser respeitado", declarou a legenda.

"Passada a eleição, é hora de encerrar a disputa e pensar nos enormes desafios que se colocam diante do nosso país. A eleição terminou. O Brasil continua, e precisa de todos nós", afirmou o presidente nacional do partido, Antonio Rueda.

O presidente nacional do PSDB, Aécio Neves, também classificou como "incompreensível" o comportamento de Flávio Bolsonaro, derrotado nas urnas.

"O exercício da oposição numa democracia é tão relevante quanto o exercício dos próprios governos. E ele deve se dar em território nacional, fiscalizando os atos do governo e cobrando os compromissos por ele assumidos com a população [...] Mas tudo isso tem que ser feito dentro das regras da democracia, com respeito às instituições e ao processo eleitoral".

O MDB também divulgou uma manifestação em defesa do resultado. "O MDB reafirma sua total confiança no sistema eleitoral brasileiro e, portanto, na legitimidade do resultado do pleito do último domingo", afirmou o partido.

O Partido da Causa Operária (PCO) reconheceu a vitória de Lula, mas também publicou manifestações nas quais afirma que Flávio Bolsonaro é perseguido pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

O partido Missão também foi considerado no levantamento. Embora não tenha publicado uma manifestação direta da legenda reconhecendo a vitória, seu presidente, Renan Santos, deu entrevistas comentando o resultado eleitoral.

O PRTB , por sua vez, anunciou que passará a se chamar Brasileiro e que pretende construir uma terceira via após a vitória de Lula.

O Partido Comunista Brasileiro (PCB), afirmou que a vitória do petista nas urnas "trata-se de um acontecimento que ultrapassa os limites de uma disputa eleitoral e assume um significado político e geopolítico de grande dimensão".

O partido Democrata publicou uma nota na qual afirma que a legenda reconhece o resultado. "Até agora não tínhamos emitido nota porque achamos desnecessário concordar com o que já é válido. Eleição válida não precisa de nota de partido para valer".

"Democracia é aceitar as regras antes da disputa e respeitar o resultado depois dela, ganhe quem ganhar. Todos os lados participaram, com a fiscalização da Justiça Eleitoral. O DEMOCRATA também disputou, com chapa própria à Presidência da República. Não vencemos, e respeitamos o resultado, como se espera de quem entra numa disputa democrática", diz a nota assinada pelo presidente do partido Suêd Haidar.

O presidente do Democracia Cristã (DC), João Caldas, afirmou que o partido reconhece o resultado da eleição. "Quem ganha, vai para o governo. Quem perde, vai para a oposição. Se alguém não concorda com algo, tem o caminho judicial."

Em nota, o PP afirmou que "reconhece o resultado das urnas e seguirá empenhado em garantir um Brasil mais próspero e seguro".

Por meio da assessoria, o Partido Renovação Democrática (PRD) afirmou que reconhece o resultado e que divulgará nota nas redes sociais.

Também através da assessoria, o Solidariedade declarou reconhecer a vitória de Lula, acrescentando que divulgará um post nas redes sociais.

O Novo adotou uma posição crítica e publicou uma manifestação afirmando que Lula utilizou a máquina pública para se reeleger e levantando questionamentos sobre o regime democrático brasileiro.

"Como se não bastasse fazer uma campanha cheia de mentiras, o PT usou como nunca a máquina pública e o STF para se manter no poder. Temos três ações pedindo a cassação da chapa de Lula", diz a publicação.

articles.title: Monark: STF arquiva inquérito após pagamento de R$ 300 mil em multa | G1
articles.standfirst: Moraes atendeu a pedido da PGR pelo arquivamento da investigação por descumprimento de decisão judicial por parte do podcaster Bruno Aiub.
articles.summary: Monark teve o inquérito no STF arquivado por Alexandre de Moraes após pagar multa de R$ 300 mil por descumprir ordens judiciais e publicar desinformação.
articles.body:
O ministro Alexandre de Moraes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal, determinou nesta quinta-feira (29) o arquivamento do inquérito que investigava o influencer Bruno Aiub , conhecido como Monark, por descumprimento de decisão judicial .

Moraes atendeu a um pedido da Procuradoria-Geral da República, que considerou que a aplicação e o pagamento de uma multa de R$ 300 mil era a sanção adequada para o caso.

O inquérito foi aberto em 2023 depois que o influencer criou novos perfis para reproduzir conteúdo com desinformação já vedado pelo STF e tentou lucrar com o material.

O podcaster fazia declarações públicas questionando, sem provas, a lisura do processo eleitoral brasileiro, a confiabilidade das urnas eletrônicas, além da atuação do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral e do próprio Supremo.

Monark teve contas bloqueadas em desdobramento da investigação sobre os atos antidemocráticos de 8 de janeiro de 2023 – quando as sedes dos Três Poderes foram invadidas e depredadas.

O procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet , reconheceu que houve violação de decisões judiciais, mas entendeu que não há justificativa para a abertura de uma ação penal.

"Na espécie, não obstante tenha sido evidenciado o descumprimento, pelo investigado Bruno Monteiro Aiub, da medida cautelar de abstenção de publicação, promoção, replicação e compartilhamento das notícias fraudulentas e antidemocráticas, houve a previsão e efetiva aplicação de multa diária pelo referido descumprimento", disse Gonet.

Segundo a Procuradoria, "assim, observa-se que o descumprimento da medida foi tratado e exaurido nos autos em que proferidas as ordens judiciais, nos quais houve aplicação de sanção específica, consistente em multa diária".

"Não há, portanto, justa causa apta a deflagração de persecução penal autônoma em relação ao referido descumprimento", concluiu o Ministério Público.

O podcaster Bruno Aiub, conhecido como Monark — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

articles.title: Só um dos 15 aliados que estavam ao lado de Flávio no discurso após eleição reproduziu carta nas redes; maioria se calou | G1
articles.standfirst: O g1 compilou as declarações sobre a carta divulgada por Flávio entre os 15 aliados ao lado do candidato derrotado e dos 17 ao lado de Lula em seus discursos após a eleição.
articles.summary: O g1 compilou as declarações sobre a carta divulgada por Flávio entre os 15 aliados ao lado do candidato derrotado e dos 17 ao lado de Lula em seus discursos após a eleição.
articles.body:
Veja quem estava com Flávio Bolsonaro em discurso da derrota — Foto: Reuters

Apenas um dos 15 aliados que estavam ao lado de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) em seu discurso após a derrota na votação, no domingo (25), reproduziu nas redes sociais a carta publicada pelo senador na quarta-feira (28). No texto, ele se dizia "presidente eleito", e depois alterou o trecho para "líder do Brasil".

José Medeiros (PL-MT), publicou em suas redes sociais, e ainda mantém no ar, a primeira versão, em que Flávio se proclama "presidente eleito".

Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) fez apenas uma citação sobre a repercussão do termo "autodeclaração", sem comentar o teor do texto. Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) negou as alegações de fraude nas urnas da carta e disse que houve "erro de confecção" no texto.

Nenhum dos outros aliados endossou o trecho inicial da carta em que Flávio falava de si como "presidente eleito" e alegava fraude eleitoral. A maior parte não comentou sobre a carta nas redes

O g1 compilou abaixo as declarações feitas até o horário de publicação deste texto no Instagram, no X e em entrevistas. Os aliados listados são os que estavam ao lado de Lula e Flávio nos discursos deles logo após a divulgação do resultado do segundo turno, na noite de domingo (25).

O deputado federal não reproduziu a carta ou comentou diretamente o texto. O parlamentar apenas fez um post no X sobre a repercussão do documento nas redes sociais.

"Esquerda zuando (sic) o Flávio porque ele “se autodeclarou” presidente… então tá liberado zuar (sic) quem se autodeclara alguma coisa?", escreveu.

Nikolas já deu diversas declarações contra a autodeclaração de gênero e já foi condenado por danos morais por chamar uma mulher trans de homem.

O senador Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), ex-coordenador da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro e líder da oposição no Senado, afirmou em entrevista que acredita ter "havido algum problema na confecção" do texto.

Marinho também se distanciou na entrevista da alegação de fraude eleitoral da carta. "O PL não pode fazer essa afirmação, nem eu posso fazer essa afirmação, porque não há provas nesse sentido", ele disse.

Nas redes sociais, Marinho postou um trecho de entrevista em que concorda com o trecho da carta em que Flávio se diz um "líder", mas não comenta o resto do texto.

O senador eleito publicou em suas redes a primeira versão, em que Flávio se proclama "presidente eleito". "Urgente: Flávio emite nota após chegar aos EUA", escreveu Medeiros.

Mesmo que o próprio Flávio tenha mudado a versão da carta para se dizer "líder" em vez de "presidente", o post de Medeiros ainda estava no ar.

Alfredo Gaspar (PL) (1), vice na chapa presidencial, a ex-presidente da Caixa, Daniella Marques (4), a deputada federal Bia Kicis (5), os senadores eleitos Guilherme Derrite (PL-SP) (6) e Deltan Dallagnol (7), o deputado federal eleito Lucas Pavanato (PL-SP) (8), os governadores eleitos do Rio Grande do Sul, Luciano Zucco (PL) (9), e do Rio de Janeiro, Douglas Ruas (PL) (10), o deputado federal Hélio Lopes (PL-RJ) (11), o coach Pablo Marçal (12), o senador pelo Rio Grande do Sul, Marcel van Hattem (Novo) (13) e o advogado Frederick Wassef (14), ainda não se manifestaram nas redes sociais sobre o teor da carta.

Veja quem estava com Lula no discurso da vitória — Foto: Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

O deputado federal eleito ironizou as idas e vindas de Flávio nas últimas semanas, a viagem aos Estados Unidos, e lembrou a promessa do senador de não deixar o país.

"Flávio Bolsonaro, depois de dizer que ganharia eleição, depois que a eleição foi roubada, depois que ia aceitar o resultado, depois disse que não sairia do país e depois fugiu para os Estados Unidos clandestinamente, menos de 48 horas depois de perda eleição, acabou de se autodeclarar presidente do Brasil ."

Cortez também lembrou que a estratégia de Flávio não é nova e que já foi usada pelo venezuelano Juan Guaidó. "Tentou fazer na Venezuela, se proclamando presidente legítimo, mas foi desautorizado até pelos seus próprios apoiadores".

O senador usou as redes sociais para fazer um comentário jocoso. "Já que hoje é o dia internacional da autoproclamação, deixa eu fazer as minhas. Minha primeira autoproclamação é que o Flamengo é o campeão da Libertadores desse ano. Pouco importa o resultado com o Estudiantes, o Flamengo já é o campeão. A outra autoproclamação é que eu sou um exímio dançarino. Todos que me conhecem e já me viram dançar sabe a importância dessa autoproclamação."

O senador Humberto Costa (PT-PE) republicou um vídeo do GloboNews+ em que a jornalista Julia Dualibi comenta a carta publicada por Flávio.

"Flávio Bolsonaro vira motivo de piada na imprensa e jornalistas caem na gargalhada", escreveu.

A deputada também voltou a dizer que Flávio fugiu e comentou a mudança no tom da carta ao substituir "presidente" por "líder".

"Depois de se autoproclamar 'presidente eleito', o golpista fujão Flávio Bolsonaro agora se diz apenas 'líder' da oposição. De vergonha em vergonha, o bolsonarismo mostra sua face pusilânime", escreveu.

A ministra da Ciência e Tecnologia, Luciana Santos, apontou o tom golpista do documento. "Flávio pode reescrever a carta, mas não a vontade do povo . Lula foi reeleito nas urnas. Não vamos normalizar o golpismo. Vamos unir as forças democráticas em defesa do voto popular e da soberania do Brasil!"

O presidente do PT, Edinho Silva, compartilhou um vídeo com críticas à carta e ao tom golpista do texto.

"Seria uma carta ridícula se não tivesse o precedente dele fazer parte de uma família que carrega o histórico golpista por conta da tentativa de golpe de 8 de janeiro de 23, quando eles não aceitaram o resultado das urnas de 22", afirma o deputado.

Outros nomes, como André Janones (Rede-MG) (1), o Ministro-chefe da Secretaria-Geral da Presidência (Psol), Guilherme Boulos (Psol) (2), o governador do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles (PT) (3), a primeira-dama Janja da Silva (4), a deputada federal eleita Ana Júlia Ribeiro (PT) (5), o ministro da Saúde, Alexandre Padilha (PT) (7), o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin (9) e sua esposa, Lu Alckmin (10), a senadora eleita Marília Arraes (PDT) (11), a senadora Teresa Leitão (PT) (12), e o senador Camilo Santana (PT) (17), ainda não se manifestaram nas redes sociais sobre a carta.

articles.title: Imagens de circuito interno mostram saques suspeitos dentro do Tribunal de Contas do MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente do TCE-MT, Sérgio Ricardo de Almeida, foi preso nesta quinta (29) suspeito de participar de esquema de desvios e, segundo a PF, há indícios de que ele recebeu 'valores milionários'.
articles.summary: Presidente do TCE-MT, Sérgio Ricardo de Almeida, foi preso nesta quinta (29) suspeito de participar de esquema de desvios e, segundo a PF, há indícios de que ele recebeu 'valores milionários'.
articles.body:
A Polícia Federal (PF) afirma que o presidente do Tribunal de Contas de Mato Grosso (TCE-MT), Sergio Ricardo de Almeida, preso nesta quinta-feira (29) em operação da corporação, é suspeito de receber ilegalmente dinheiro de um esquema de desvios de recursos do tribunal.

Segundo a PF, as movimentações financeiras ilegais duraram quase um ano.

“As movimentações teriam ocorrido ao longo de mais de dez meses. Durante a investigação, foram identificados indícios de que autoridades do Tribunal, entre elas o próprio presidente, o consultor jurídico e outros conselheiros, estariam se locupletando de valores milionários provenientes da instituição”, disse a PF.

Sérgio Ricardo, presidente do Tribunal de Contas de Mato Grosso — Foto: Reprodução

Na investigação, a PF teve acesso a imagens de circuito interno, analisadas em conjunto com dados bancários.

Segundo os investigadores, essas imagens “registraram saques recorrentes de numerário por servidores e apontaram coincidências temporais entre determinados créditos e retiradas realizadas em posto de atendimento bancário localizado nas dependências da instituição”.

O presidente do Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Mato Grosso (TCE-MT), Sérgio Ricardo de Almeida, foi preso nesta quinta-feira (29) durante uma operação da Polícia Federal que investiga suspeitas de irregularidades em contratos públicos e pagamentos a servidores da instituição.

O procurador do TCE-MT, Grhegory Paiva Pires, também foi preso.

Batizada de Operação Tomada de Contas, a operação deflagrada nesta quinta-feira (29) mobilizou mais de 180 policiais federais e cumpriu seis mandados de prisão preventiva e 26 de busca e apreensão em Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul e São Paulo.

As medidas foram autorizadas pelo Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ). Além das prisões e buscas, a operação incluiu medidas para acessar informações protegidas por sigilo e bloquear bens relacionados à investigação.

articles.title: Alaska man says Democratic operative recruited him to run in Senate race
articles.summary: Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy directed the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether the effort broke Alaska law.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — An Alaska insurance manager says a man with a spoofed phone number and only a first name tried to recruit him as an independent Senate candidate, promising backing from wealthy donors he never identified.

Matthew Salisbury, a former Republican U.S. House candidate, told NewsNation's "Katie Pavlich Tonight" on Wednesday that he turned down the offer because he "could never verify who this person was."

His account follows a New York Times report that Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola's aides, campaign lawyers, and Senate Democrats' campaign arm helped recruit candidates who could siphon votes from Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. Peltola's campaign and national Democrats deny the report.

Alaska governor calls for investigation into Mary Peltola's Senate campaign

Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy directed the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether the effort broke Alaska law, saying in a post on X that the Times reporting "substantially supports" findings from a June Division of Elections investigation. "Deliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections," he said.

Salisbury said the call came "out of the blue" in December from a man who called himself Zane. The caller said he represented several wealthy donors who wanted to break the two-party system, Salisbury said, but he "would never tell me where the money was coming from."

They met twice before Salisbury decided to pass.

Salisbury said the man never disclosed a tie to Democrats.

He separately told NewsNation the Times showed him a photo of Jerid Kurtz, a Democratic operative and Peltola campaign consultant, and that Kurtz was the man he met.

NewsNation has reached out to Kurtz for comment.

Salisbury said he did not grasp the scope until reading the Times story that morning, adding "a national party is hand-selecting candidates and attempting to manipulate who actually makes the ballot."

articles.title: Johnson signals he’ll remain atop GOP, scrambling leadership landscape
articles.summary: Speaker Mike Johnson’s (R-La.) recent hints that he intends to remain GOP leader even if Republicans lose the House have rattled the party’s leadership outlo...
articles.body:
Speaker Mike Johnson's (R-La.) recent hints that he intends to remain GOP leader even if Republicans lose the House have rattled the party's leadership outlook and raised fresh new questions about the GOP's future heading into the next Congress.

Most House Speakers in recent decades have stepped out of Congress after losing the gavel. And Reps. Steve Scalise (R-La.), the majority leader, and Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), a conservative icon, are both expected to launch bids to lead House Republicans if Democrats flip the chamber, according to GOP lawmakers, aides and strategists.

But Johnson recently muddled the leadership landscape by signaling his intention to keep his spot atop the party even if Republicans are knocked out of power. Then on Monday, President Trump offered a glowing endorsement of Johnson's leadership chops, sparking further speculation that Johnson might, in fact, buck historic trends and try to remain leader even from the minority.

"Mike Johnson is a true friend, fighter, and WINNER," Trump posted on social media, "and he has my Complete and Total endorsement for Re-Election."

"Thank you, President @realDonaldTrump!" Johnson responded. "The best is yet to come as we save America!"

Much about the leadership race is expected to come into sharper focus after next Tuesday's midterm elections. A Johnson spokesperson said the Speaker is "solely focused on protecting the majority," noting that he "will campaign in 21 districts across 13 states between now and Election Day."

But many Republicans are skeptical, predicting Johnson will follow the example of past GOP Speakers — including Newt Gingrich (Ga.), Dennis Hastert (Ill.), Paul Ryan (Wis.) and Kevin McCarthy (Calif.) — who all left Capitol Hill in short order after losing the gavel.

"I highly doubt that the Speaker will go for minority leader at this point," a GOP aide said Wednesday. "I just don't see him having a desire. I don't think he's having a fun time as Speaker. I don't think he'd want to be minority leader."

Former Speaker Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) defied modern tradition in 2011, when she clung to the minority leader seat after the party was clobbered in the 2010 midterms. Pelosi would win the gavel back eight years later, but she's been the exception.

GOP strategist Amy Frederiksen said, "When you lose, and you're no longer Speaker …it's hard to go back to minority leader."

"There's certainly a lot less trappings and a lot less power, and also the caucus just tends to kind of want to clean some house. Like members just see it as an opportunity to just switch things up, and so it's not that it hasn't happened, of course. Speaker Pelosi went to be the minority leader, so it isn't unprecedented," Frederiksen said. "It wouldn't be historic in any kind of way, and it's very possible. But it is — I don't think it's as simple as him just deciding. I think that the caucus is going to really want to weigh in on things."

She added that Johnson was a "compromise candidate anyway" for Speaker.

"We went through a couple, two, three, four different potential Speakers, including Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan, when he was finally chosen as Speaker, so I, you know, I just think that there is that," she said. "It was sort of a bargain struck anyway for him to be Speaker."

Some Republicans predicted next year's leadership roster will hinge on how the midterms play out. Although Trump is not on the ballot, the elections are shaping up to be a referendum on the president, whose historic unpopularity has created huge challenges for GOP candidates and made Democrats the favorite to control the House next year.

Still, some Republicans believe that if Democrats win by a wide margin, Johnson will bear much of the blame, lose support within the conference and struggle to secure the votes needed to become minority leader, even if Trump wanted him there.

"I would imagine there to be more of a push for someone else, just given that over, you know, a billion dollars has been spent on the midterms alone," a second GOP staffer, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, told The Hill earlier this month.

Although both Scalise and Jordan have downplayed their interest in the top spot, many Republicans say they're both angling for the position, setting the stage for a potentially messy internal fight when House lawmakers return to Washington the week after the midterms. (Minnesota Rep. Tom Emmer, the Republican whip, says he wants to remain in that seat).

There's plenty of disagreement about who would have the advantage in such a race. Some say that if it's a two-way race between Scalise and Jordan, Scalise would likely be better positioned than Jordan to step into the top spot given his current leadership position.

"I think for Scalise … it'd be an easy transition for him to step into that. But for Jordan, he's really — how do I phrase this? He's been a loyal soldier. He's rallied people well, and he's an effective politician. So I think both would do well in the role, but I think Scalise would have an easier transition just out of pure — his House leadership currently," a third GOP staffer said.

The first Republican staffer, though, predicted Jordan has the edge.

"He's done a lot of work over the past couple years where he's kind of built his own coalition, [and] he does have, like, a cult following around the country when he goes on the campaign trail. So I do think it's his to lose at this point," the first aide said. "When you're in the minority, you need somebody who can be a fighter and willing to go out there and go on TV and bomb some bombs. And I think he's the guy for it."

The offices of Scalise and Jordan did not respond to requests for comment on Wednesday.

Johnson has faced a rocky tenure as Speaker, often marked by internal GOP fighting, a razor-thin margin and repeated challenges in keeping his conference united on government spending, the Iran war and other issues.

Even so, Johnson told CBS News's Robert Costa this month that in the "unlikely scenario" Republicans lose the House, "I would expect my colleagues would ask me to continue leading this conference, even if we have divided government."

"I'm going to continue to serve my highest best use to God and country, and I believe right now, as we're sitting here, that's the Speaker of the House," Johnson said. "And if we lost the majority, I don't think that that position that I have would change. I think I would stay right there."

Some Republicans note that if Johnson were to jump into the minority leader race, he would have a strong case for the position.

The third GOP staffer noted Johnson's "had to deal with a lot of curveballs" and that he's handled them well.

"I think that the party recognizes that and will react accordingly," the staffer said. "That doesn't mean there's not people gunning for the same spot, but I think Johnson has been a good leader, a team player amidst what is, you know — we could say honestly — has been some chaos at times."

articles.title: Donald Trump Reportedly Hiding ‘Near-Constant Contact’ Exchange With Aide Natalie Harp In Federal Case
articles.summary: Donald Trump is facing accusations of trying to keep communications involving Natalie Harp under wraps as the legal battle over […]
articles.body:
Donald Trump is facing accusations of trying to keep communications involving Natalie Harp under wraps as the legal battle over the Kennedy Center's shutdown intensifies.

A new court filing has highlighted messages between Trump's aide and the Kennedy Center's leadership, and lawyers are now seeking to have them released.

The legal move comes as the president's close relationship with his executive assistant and their public interaction face growing scrutiny.

Donald Trump Accused of Hiding Communications Of His Aide Linked To Kennedy Center Closure

Lawyers representing Joyce Beatty, a former member of the Kennedy Center's board, have asked a judge to compel the Trump administration to release withheld messages and documents related to the decision to close the renowned arts venue.

The October 25 filing points to communications that Beatty's legal team believes could clarify the administration's involvement in the shutdown.

According to the complaint, 19 text messages were passed between Harp and the center's chief executive Matt Floca. Eleven of them were exchanged on the day the board convened for a third meeting to approve the closure.

Beatty's attorneys allege that Trump's team has sought to keep the exchanges private by claiming they were privileged presidential communications.

However, they argue that the messages, particularly those involving Harp, show "near-constant contact" between Trump's associates and the venue's leadership as plans for the closure progressed.

The legal team also accused the administration of potentially engaging in "gamesmanship" by restricting access to relevant records.

"Without access to these materials, (Beatty) will lack a complete picture of Defendants' actions," the filing read, per Irish Star .

Reason Behind Natalie Harp's Loyalty To Donald Trump Exposed

The allegations of Trump's attempt to hide his aide's messages come amid intense scrutiny of his relationship with her.

The Blast recently reported that Natalie's brother, Preston Harp, offered insight into what may explain her strong loyalty to the president. He suggested that their father's death may have deepened her emotional attachment to Trump.

A 2023 letter Harp wrote to the 80-year-old further highlighted the personal significance of their connection. She thanked him for his support as she continued to cope with the loss of her father.

Similarly, Trump's gestures towards Harp have also seemingly pointed to their bond. On October 7, he appeared to wait for his executive assistant after they landed, with one reporter noting that he kept "glancing back" to the helicopter before she came out.

Donald Trump And Natalie Harp's Connection Raised Concerns About His Wife Melania Trump

Another exchange between Trump and Harp has also added to the speculation. At a rally in Nebraska on October 5, Trump publicly praised her while signing an executive order aimed at reducing diesel prices.

He called her to the stage to bring the document and described her as a "perfect person," joking that the exchange could easily become a television show.

The clip soon went mainstream, sparking criticism from viewers. Some questioned his relationship with Harp, while others pointed out that he had never spoken about Melania in such terms.

As The Blast reported, MS NOW's Lawrence O'Donnell weighed in on Trump's remarks, saying he has "never said those three words about the current Mrs.Donald Trump."

How Donald Trump's Daughter Ivanka Reportedly Views Harp's Closeness To Her Father

While reactions poured in, one person close to the billionaire mogul who is not thrilled about his connection to his assistant is his daughter Ivanka Trump .

"Ivanka hates her," one source said. They added that Harp appears to have stepped into a role Ivanka once filled, regularly accompanying Trump and drawing his attention.

The insider also claims that adding to the discord is that Ivanka believes Harp has begun copying her looks, pointing to blonde hair, fashion choices, and a polished style.

Poll Revealed Voters Want Answers About Natalie Harp's Role In Trump's Inner Circle

As questions surrounding Natalie Harp's closeness to Trump continue to mount, a poll suggests that many voters want greater clarity about the 35-year-old's background and influence within the president's inner circle.

According to findings reported by The Blast , 42% of registered voters believe important questions about Harp remain unanswered.

Support for greater transparency was particularly strong among Democrats, 58% of whom wanted more information, while just 13% felt no further details were necessary.

Republicans were more divided, with 29% seeking answers and 35% opposing additional scrutiny.

articles.title: Trump’s midterm reckoning: Why the Republican Party is facing a Senate wipeout
articles.summary: A year ago, losing control of the Senate seemed rather unlikely for Republicans. Today, the fact that their Senate majority is in doubt at all is a major rebuke.
articles.body:
You can tell when President Trump knows he is in trouble. Of course, he’ll never admit to making a mistake. If there is something everyone should know by now, it’s that Trump will never admit he is wrong, never admit he lost and never apologizes.

But over the past few weeks, Trump has clearly signaled he recognizes that he has not taken inflation seriously enough — the trade fight with Canada was ill-timed, to say the least — and he picked some real duds to run for Senate.

Although he deserves some credit for recognizing his errors , in marked contrast to the Biden administration’s denial and delusion, it is too late to fix his mistakes. Despite the copious copium dished out by various conservative-leaning pundits over bad polls and fake news, and what is really a favorable Senate map, Republicans are more likely than not to lose control of the Senate in addition to their majority in the House .

A year ago, losing control of the Senate seemed rather unlikely for Republicans. The only seat in a state where Trump lost in 2024 was Maine , where Sen. Susan Collins (R) has proven to be the ultimate political survivor. At the same time, Democrats were defending seats in two states Trump won — Georgia and Michigan. Even if Trump and the Republicans faced a typical first-term downer cycle, losing the majority seemed inconceivable.

If every Republican in every state ran 10 points behind 2024 Trump, Republicans would lose only Maine and North Carolina. That is a monumental structural advantage. Trump’s winning margin in the seats that are now viewed as competitive ranged from 11.2 percent (Ohio) to 17.9 percent (South Carolina). Yet according to the RealClearPolitics averages , Democratic candidates are winning in all the 2024 competitive and Democratic states, as well as in Ohio, Alaska (plus-13.1 percent for Trump) and Texas (plus-13.7 percent for Trump).

There are enough close races that the final tally for the Senate could be anywhere from a 53-47 Republican majority (no change) to a 55-45 Democratic wipeout. It is increasingly looking like at least a slim Democratic majority. At the time of writing, the RealClear “no toss-ups” map is 52-48 for Democrats. With their seven toss-ups, RealClear has it at 47-44, Sabato’s Crystal Ball shows 49-46, with five toss-ups, and Cook Politico Report is at 47-46, with seven toss-ups.

The challenge in projecting the final numbers is that none of the Democrats in competitive races are consistently polling at or above 50 percent. That means undecided voters will make the difference — most of those undecided voters were 2024 Trump voters. That bit of data is what gives Trump and Republican leaders’ confidence.

The problem with that reasoning, however, is that those undecideds must both turn out and not turn against the Republicans.

Consider Ohio, where Trump won by more than 11 points. Former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D) leads current Sen. Jon Husted (R) — appointed to the JD Vance vacancy — 48.1 to 44.8 percent, with 7.1 percent undecided, in the RealClear average. If you accept the polling, then for Husted to overtake Brown, he would need to win 75 percent of undecided voters — and that’s if they actually vote. If only half the undecided voters turn out, Husted loses.

The situation is brighter in Texas, with Democratic state Rep. James Talarico having just a 1.8 percent RealClear advantage and 4.8 percent undecided. Republican Ken Paxton needs 71 percent of the undecided voters. If only half the undecided voters turn out, Paxton loses. The narrower lead does mean that more polls are within the margin of error. Paxton might be closer than reported. But margin of error works both ways.

Yes, the polls might be off, but that does not track with the national mood. The right direction-wrong track is net negative by more than 31 points. Trump’s RealClear average approval is negative by almost 22 points. Even Trump-friendly polls show the president lagging, with Rasmussen at negative 16 points, Morning Consult down 17 points and RMG Research down 15 points. The most Trump-friendly of them all, Harvard-Harris, has Trump down 20 points. A systemic polling error of 1 point in the Republicans’ favor (which is a lot), would still leave Democrats leading most races and Republicans relying on turning out sour voters.

It is possible Republicans will hang on to 50 or 51 seats. Abdul El-Sayed is a bad candidate in Michigan, stubbornly stuck at about a 2-point lead . The New York Times story on Mary Peltola’s skullduggery could be enough to boost the real Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) in Alaska. Troy Jackson is a weak candidate in Maine against Collins.

But the fact that their Senate majority is in doubt at all is a major rebuke to Republicans. A new Senate with a bare Republican majority would still feature unreliables like Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska), the prickly Rand Paul (R-Ky.) and the wildcard John Fetterman (D-Pa.). And all that with a president who maybe-not-so-secretly thinks he should be able to run again and certainly is not interested in relinquishing any power.

Regardless of the results on Tuesday, it will be a raucous, fractious couple of years.

Keith Naughton is a former campaign consultant and co-founder of the public affairs firm Silent Majority Strategies. Find him on his Substack, “Betting On Politics.”

articles.title: Hegseth fires top Pentagon strategist accused of leaking classified Iran, Ukraine war information
articles.summary: Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia allegedly failed three polygraph exams tied to classified leaks about the Iran war and Ukraine before Pete Hegseth fired him.
articles.body: War Secretary Pete Hegseth fired one of the Pentagon’s senior strategic planners amid an investigation into allegations he leaked classified information to journalists about the Iran war, Russia’s war in Ukraine and other sensitive matters, a Department of War official told Fox News. The official said Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia failed three polygraph examinations related to alleged disclosures of classified information. The investigation has been referred to the Justice Department. Sylvia is also accused of meeting journalists outside the Pentagon with the alleged intention of leaking classified material after Hegseth imposed new media restrictions requiring reporters to be escorted inside the building. HEGSETH ANNOUNCES JOINT TASK FORCE WITH DOJ TO PROSECUTE LEAKS TO JOURNALISTS 'WITH THE FULL FORCE OF THE LAW' Fox News Digital has reached out to Sylvia for comment but did not hear back at time of publication. The Justice Department declined to comment specifically on Sylvia but said it has "ongoing investigations related to possible leaks of classified information" and works closely with the Department of War. Pentagon chief spokesman Sean Parnell said the personnel action followed "an extensive Air Force OSI investigation," though he did not identify Sylvia by name in his statement or provide further details about the investigation. Parnell issued a pointed warning to those suspected of leaking classified information: "Our commitment was not an empty promise. We vowed to find you, and we meant it." Sylvia served as director of the Joint Staff’s Directorate for Strategy, Plans and Policy, known as the J5, a senior role responsible for developing military strategy and advising the chairman of the Joint Chiefs. The J5 has been sidelined from that role since the spring, according to well-placed sources who spoke to Fox News. The official stressed that Sylvia was not a central planner of the Iran war, which falls under U.S. Central Command and its commander, Adm. Brad Cooper. The Atlantic first reported Sylvia’s ouster Wednesday night, citing sources who said Hegseth had lost confidence in the three-star general amid tensions with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby. Sylvia is the second officer leading the J5 to be removed under Hegseth, following Lt. Gen. Joseph McGee. Hegseth also removed Lt. Gen. Douglas Sims, then director of the Joint Staff, earlier this year. President Donald Trump told reporters Sylvia is going to have "big problems, long term problems" on Thursday. Hegseth has previously alleged leaks within his own senior ranks. Three Pentagon officials were removed amid a leak investigation last year, though they denied wrongdoing and said they were never told what they were accused of leaking. The abrupt removal comes as the Pentagon reportedly weighs renewed military action against Iran. PENTAGON RACES TO BUY 10X MORE MISSILES AS IRAN WAR DWINDLES ARSENAL, THREATENS READINESS FOR CHINA AGGRESSION U.S. officials have reportedly warned allies in the Middle East to prepare for possible renewed strikes after next week’s midterm elections and potential Iranian retaliation, while additional U.S. forces are moving into the region. A 1994 West Point graduate, Sylvia has served more than three decades in the Army, including multiple deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, and was wounded in combat. Before taking over the J5 in December, he commanded the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell and had previously served as the J5’s vice director. articles.title: Scalise stresses voter turnout: ‘We can hold the House’
articles.summary: House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) on Wednesday stressed that Republicans could hold on to their control of the House if there’s strong voter turnout on Election Day. NewsNation’s Katie Pavlich asked Scalise if he was preparing for a Democrat-led House that would look to investigate President Trump and his family or impeach Trump for…
articles.body:
House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) on Wednesday stressed that Republicans could hold on to their control of the House if there’s strong voter turnout on Election Day.

NewsNation’s Katie Pavlich asked Scalise if he was preparing for a Democrat-led House that would look to investigate President Trump and his family or impeach Trump for a third time between his two terms.

“Katie, we know this, and that is number one, there are a lot of close races right now, and if good people stay home, socialists can absolutely win some of these seats,” Scalise said during an appearance on “Katie Pavlich Tonight.”

“And that’s why the biggest thing we’re doing right now is encouraging people to turn out and vote, because if folks that normally sit out of midterm actually show up and vote this time around, we can hold the House,” he continued.

Scalise added that if “good people stay at home, you’re seeing these crazy far-left socialist candidates –– they hate President Trump. They vowed retribution. They want to go after the president, go after his family.”

Pavlich noted that the odds of the GOP keeping a lock on the House were “razor-thin,” and she asked if the Louisiana Republican was looking at any of the toss-up races that could determine which party controls the lower chamber.

The lawmaker said these races could be wins for Republicans “if folks show up.”

Pollster Nate Silver said Sunday that midterm polling “ would have to be very wrong ” for the GOP to hold their control of the House, explaining that the tougher battle for Democrats would be winning states won by Trump in 2024 to attain control of the Senate.

Polling firms have largely leaned toward a likely Democratic victory in the House, an outcome The Hill’s election partner Decision Desk HQ projects with 80 percent probability.

This potential outcome will likely stand as a referendum on Trump’s first two years back in the White House, similar to most midterm election results when the opposing party takes control of one or both chambers of Congress.

Trump has also encouraged high turnout, urging GOP voters to “pretend” he’s on the ballot. The president has touted his administration’s successes while out stumping for candidates across the country in recent weeks, but consistent polling has shown growing dissatisfaction with his handling of the presidency and not prioritizing issues like the economy and the cost of living.

Midterm elections generally see a lower voter turnout compared with years when there’s a presidential election. The 2020 and 2024 presidential elections saw some of the highest turnout of voters in the last century, with rates at 66 and 64 percent, respectively, according to the Pew Research Center .

The 2018 and 2022 midterm cycles, however, saw turnout of less than 50 percent, specifically at 49 percent and 46 percent, respectively, Pew reported . But the 2018 midterms saw the highest turnout rate since 1914, and 2022’s turnout exceeded that of any midterm since 1970.

articles.title: Democrats leading in Texas, Michigan Senate races: Polling
articles.summary: Democrats are leading in the Texas and Michigan Senate races, according to new polling. The CNN polls released Thursday found 49 percent of respondents backed or leaned toward Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, while 42 percent said the same of Republican Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race. Five percent said they didn’t back either candidate, 3…
articles.body:
Democrats are leading in the Texas and Michigan Senate races, according to new polling .

The CNN polls released Thursday found 49 percent of respondents backed or leaned toward Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, while 42 percent said the same of Republican Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race. Five percent said they didn’t back either candidate, 3 percent backed or leaned toward another candidate and 1 percent had “no opinion.”

In Texas, 49 percent of respondents backed or leaned toward Democrat James Talarico, while 43 percent went with Republican Ken Paxton. Five percent said they didn’t back either candidate, and 3 percent backed or leaned toward supporting someone else.

The Michigan and Texas Senate races are among the most-watched elections this year, with the Wolverine State’s status as a swing state and Democrats long eyeing a statewide win in the Lone Star State.

Democrats are also dealing with a friendly political environment this cycle, with issues like the Iran war, President Trump’s sagging approval rating and concerns about the cost of living weighing the GOP down.

In the Texas poll, 59 percent said they “disapprove” of Trump’s job performance, and 41 percent said they “approve” of his work. In Michigan, 66 percent said they were down on the president’s job performance, while 33 percent approved of it. One percent in the Wolverine State had “no opinion” on Trump’s work in his role.

Trump’s national approval rating was sitting at 38.7 percent on Thursday morning, according to a polling average from The Hill’s partner Decision Desk HQ, with his disapproval rating at 59.3 percent.

The CNN polls in Texas and Michigan took place from Oct. 20-27, featuring 768 Michigan registered voters and 923 Texas registered voters. The Michigan poll’s margin of error was 4.7 percentage points, while the Texas poll’s was 4.2 percentage points.

articles.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) said Wednesday she is still supporting Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed after her fiance announced he would back the GOP candidate, former Rep. Mike Rogers (Mich.), in the contest. “Like a lot of households in America, we’re a household divided,” she told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins. “I still very much want…
articles.body:
Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) said Wednesday she is still supporting Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed after her fiance announced he would back the GOP candidate, former Rep. Mike Rogers (Mich.), in the contest.

“Like a lot of households in America, we’re a household divided,” she told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins. “I still very much want our Democratic nominee, his name is Abdul, to win this race.”

Stevens publicly backed El-Sayed in the race after he narrowly defeated her in Michigan’s August Democratic primary.

This week, her former campaign chair David Kramer and her fiance, Jason Turkish, said they would not support the Democrat over comments they deemed as antisemitic. Both men said they would vote for Rogers instead.

In a Wednesday interview with The Detroit News , Turkish said he has witnessed an “escalation” in El-Sayed’s rhetoric since his primary win.

“We have never seen a candidate for U.S. Senate act so recklessly toward the safety of Jews in the community as we have seen from Abdul,” the Jewish Democratic donor said.

Turkish also told the outlet he planned to attend the Republican Jewish Coalition’s Wednesday evening event in Birmingham, Mich., titled “Who Will Keep Us Safe? Rogers vs. El-Sayed.” The panel featured the Republican candidate and Texas Sen. Ted Cruz (R).

El-Sayed has faced criticism for a political ad supporting his campaign that appeared to blame Israel and Jews for rising costs of living. The Democratic candidate said the ad was not affiliated with his campaign.

Still, Rogers accused his Democratic opponent of using language that “invites anti-Semitism — and violence against Jews” in a Wednesday post on the social platform X.

Jewish leaders in Michigan also urged El-Sayed this week to take down a separate ad featuring conservative pundit Tucker Carlson, who has a history of antisemitic rhetoric.

Additionally, the progressive candidate has faced pushback for his repeated criticism of the Israeli government’s military operations in Gaza following Hamas’s attack on Oct. 7, 2023.

While Stevens told CNN she still supports El-Sayed’s bid, she said she’s heard concerns from voters about his rhetoric on the campaign trail.

“I will be honest, there are a lot of voters in Michigan … and they are still undecided and they are hurt and they are confused,” she told Collins. “And this is why I think our nominee is in a very strong position to denounce the hateful ads that have hurt people.”

Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed earlier this year, urged the Democratic candidate, with whom she has not publicly campaigned in months, to “shut out the hate.”

“Let’s get these undecided voters over the finish line,” she continued. “Let’s make sure that Michigan has the representation it needs in the United States Senate.”

articles.title: Selective sanctuary: America’s ‘White South Africans Only’ refugee policy is wrong
articles.summary: As persecution continues around the world, so too should our bipartisan support for refugees — regardless of where they come from, the color of their skin, or what faith they practice.
articles.body:
On the first day of his second term, President Trump issued an executive order titled “ Realigning the United States Refugee Admissions Program .” That decades-long program, which historically enjoyed broad bipartisan support, provides a legal way for refugees fleeing persecution in other countries to be rigorously vetted and, if approved, resettled in the United States.

The executive order, which remains in effect, amounts to an indefinite refugee ban, suspending the program “until such time as the further entry into the United States of refugees aligns with the interests of the United States.” Since then, the administration has allowed for exceptions to the ban, but almost exclusively for white South Africans.

The Trump administration made its priorities clear a year ago, on Oct. 30, 2025, when it announced it would limit the number of refugees admitted annually to the U.S. to a historic low of 7,500, almost all of them white South Africans. Then, in May, the administration announced that it would admit an additional 10,000 white South Africans into the U.S. as refugees this year, while still blocking people from essentially all other countries from entering through the program.

According to data released by the U.S. Department of State in October, the U.S. accepted a total of 16,292 refugees in fiscal 2026. All but five of them are South Africans .

Trump is required by law to issue a determination of the target on legal refugees before the start of each new federal fiscal year. On Sept. 25, 2026, he issued a Presidential Determination capping refugee admissions in the new fiscal year at 17,500, primarily for Afrikaners from South Africa. No other country was mentioned.

The new admissions limit and the pattern of focusing on just one refugee group represents a stark change in a humanitarian program that had previously provided a vital haven for refugees from a wide range of persecutions and countries. In 1982, Ronald Reagan set the annual ceiling at 140,000; in 2024, the Biden administration set a target of 125,000 .

The federal government’s single-minded focus on Afrikaners has categorically and unlawfully blocked vulnerable refugees from other populations and deprived them of the chance of even applying for an exception to the refugee ban. It even eliminates the priorities set by Congress, which include the Follow-to-Join Program for spouses and minor children of refugees in the U.S.; the Iraqi Direct Access Program for U.S.-affiliated Iraqis; and the Lautenberg Program for persecuted religious minorities, including 14,000 individuals who are currently at risk amid escalating violence in Iran.

Meanwhile, a legal challenge to the ban continues in the courts. On April 7, Church World Service, along with HIAS , Lutheran Community Services Northwest and several refugee plaintiffs moved to file an amended complaint in our ongoing lawsuit challenging the refugee ban. The amended complaint alleges that the administration’s exclusion of all refugees except for South Africans is driven by racial animus and brings a new focus on refugee populations prioritized by Congress that continue to be barred.

Among the refugees stranded in the pipeline overseas are those who have received support from the Republican-controlled Congress, and even from within the administration. The Lautenberg Program was included in the annual appropriations bill for the U.S. State Department signed by Trump in 2026. And the Senate version of the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act includes a provision protecting Afghan allies stranded at a former U.S. military base in Qatar, many of whom have already been approved for refugee resettlement.

America has a long history of welcoming those fleeing persecution. But this administration has ended the U.S. refugee program as we know it: dismantling protections, maintaining a refugee ban, and resettling almost exclusively white people from a single country of origin.

At Church World Service, we continue to fight for an end to the refugee ban and for the resettlement of those being kept unlawfully in limbo. We call for a more equitable, inclusive admissions program that will keep its promises to those left stranded in extremely dangerous circumstances.

At a minimum, the administration should broaden exceptions to the ban beyond South Africans. And as Trump added 10,000 white South Africans midway through the last fiscal year, so he has discretion to consult with Congress and adjust the latest limits during the current fiscal year.

As persecution continues around the world, so too should our bipartisan support for refugees — regardless of where they come from, the color of their skin, or what faith they practice.

Rick Santos is president and chief executive officer of Church World Service , a faith-based humanitarian and social justice organization.
